::: {.callout-important}
## Read this before you start

Six sections, one for each question that was marked wrong. Each section tests the **method** from the clinic,
not the same numbers. Before each section, re-read its **Memorise this box** in the
**[clinic](tyler_exam_set_a_p2_only_for_woonju.qmd)**.

The six habits being tested:

| | the habit |
|---|---|
| **A** | over/under for the trapezium rule comes from the sign of $f''$, and "underestimate" is the weaker condition |
| **B** | factorise the discriminant, build the whole map once, then test every option against it |
| **C** | write the domain down first; $a\log_b x=\log_b x^{a}$ needs $x>0$ |
| **D** | SSA: check $h<a<c$, cosine rule on the given angle, area ratio = ratio of the roots |
| **E** | necessary means the **larger** set — draw the intervals before counting |
| **F** | translate to symbols, flip **every** quantifier in order, negate the final condition |
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Answer form.** Necessary/sufficient questions → name which, and say why the other direction fails.
Ranges → an inequality or interval, with each endpoint stated as included or excluded. Negations → the
symbolic form **and** the English. Numerical answers → exact values, not decimals.

**Total: 48 marks.**
:::

# Section C — Logarithms: domain and equivalence

## Question 6 &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.78em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">[5 marks]</span>

::: {.question}
A student solves $\log_2(7x-3)=1+2\log_2(x-1)$ as follows.

| | |
|---|---|
| Step 1 | $\log_2(7x-3)-2\log_2(x-1)=1$ |
| Step 2 | $\log_2(7x-3)-\log_2\bigl((x-1)^{2}\bigr)=1$ |
| Step 3 | $\dfrac{7x-3}{(x-1)^{2}}=2$ |
| Step 4 | $2x^{2}-11x+5=0$ |
| Step 5 | $(2x-1)(x-5)=0$ |
| Step 6 | $x=\tfrac12$ or $x=5$ |

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(a)** State the domain of the original equation.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(b)** Identify the **first** step at which the solution set changes, and prove it by showing a
value that satisfies that step but not the one before it.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**(c)** Give the correct solution.
:::

## Before you hand it in

- [ ] Every necessary/sufficient answer argues **both** directions, with a counterexample for the one that
      fails.
- [ ] Every range answer says explicitly whether each endpoint is in or out.
- [ ] Every log question starts with the domain, written down before any algebra.
- [ ] Every SSA question checks $h<a<c$ before solving anything.
- [ ] Every negation flips **all** the quantifiers, keeps their order, and negates the final condition.
- [ ] No decimals where an exact value was available.
:::
